pt-reis.kid: On the sixth of January, Christians remember the three wise men. They followed a bright star and brought gifts to baby Jesus. In Portugal, people eat a king cake. It is round, with a hole in the middle. It has sugary fruit on top, like jewels on a crown. A dried bean was hidden in the cake. Whoever found it had to buy the cake the next year. At the start of January, people also go from house to house. They sing old songs called “janeiras”.
pt-reis.q: What was traditionally hidden in the king cake?
pt-reis.draw: Draw a round king cake with colourful sugary fruit and a crown next to it

pt-carnaval.kid: Carnival is a fun party before Lent, the quiet time before Easter. Everyone dresses up in costumes and masks. Loud parades with music and drums go through the streets. Children come to nursery and school in costumes. They have their own parade too. The most famous carnival in Portugal is in the town of Torres Vedras. By tradition, many people do not work on the Tuesday of carnival. But it is not an official holiday.
pt-carnaval.q: What do the children wear when they go to school at carnival?
pt-carnaval.draw: Draw yourself in a carnival costume and mask

pt-sexta-santa.kid: Good Friday is a quiet, sad day before Easter. Christians remember how Jesus was hurt and died on the cross. On this day the church bells do not ring. Many families do not eat meat. They cook fish instead. Christians know that in two days it will be Easter, the happiest holiday. In Portugal this is a day off.
pt-sexta-santa.q: What do many families cook on this day instead of meat?
pt-sexta-santa.draw: Draw a lit candle and the first spring flowers

pt-pascoa.kid: Easter is the happiest holiday for Christians. They believe that Jesus rose again. That means he came back to life. In Portugal, godparents give their godchildren a “folar”. It is a special bread, and sometimes whole eggs are baked inside it. On the table there are little dishes of sugared almonds. Children get chocolate eggs. The whole family comes together for a big lunch.
pt-pascoa.q: What do godparents give their godchildren at Easter in Portugal?
pt-pascoa.draw: Draw a special bread with eggs baked in it

pt-dia-pai.kid: On the nineteenth of March, Portugal celebrates Father’s Day. It is the day of Saint Joseph. He was Mary’s husband, and he looked after baby Jesus like a real dad. Joseph was a carpenter, so you often see him with tools. At school, children make gifts and cards. At home they give Dads and grandpas big hugs.
pt-dia-pai.q: What job did Saint Joseph do?
pt-dia-pai.draw: Draw a card for Dad with what he loves most

pt-25-abril.kid: More than fifty years ago, Portugal was not free. People could not say what they thought. They could not choose who ran the country. On the twenty-fifth of April, soldiers took over the government with almost no fighting. People gave them red carnations, and the soldiers put the flowers in their guns. So this day is called the Carnation Revolution and Freedom Day. Today people go out into the streets with red carnations and sing songs about freedom.
pt-25-abril.q: What flowers did people give to the soldiers?

pt-trabalhador.kid: The first of May is a holiday for everyone who works: doctors, teachers, builders, cooks and drivers. In Portugal it is a day off, and people rest with their families. In towns there are parades with flags. In some villages, people put twigs of yellow flowers on doors and windows. That is how they say hello to spring.
pt-trabalhador.q: What do people in villages put on their doors at the start of May?
pt-trabalhador.draw: Draw a door with twigs of yellow flowers on it

pt-dia-mae.kid: On the first Sunday of May, Portugal celebrates Mother’s Day. Children make cards and gifts for their mums with their hands. Some bring Mum breakfast in bed. Many families go for a walk or have lunch together. Grannies are mums too, so you can phone them and wish them a happy day!
pt-dia-mae.q: What can you bring Mum in the morning on this day?
pt-dia-mae.draw: Draw a bunch of flowers for Mum

pt-crianca.kid: On the first of June, many countries celebrate Children’s Protection Day. In Portugal it is called World Children’s Day. On this day grown-ups remind us that every child needs to be healthy, to learn and to play. Schools, parks and towns have games, plays and parties. Many children get small gifts.
pt-crianca.q: What is the holiday of the first of June called in Portugal?
pt-crianca.draw: Draw yourself and your friends at a party with balloons

pt-corpo-deus.kid: Corpus Christi is always on a Thursday, two months after Easter. It is about the last supper of Jesus and his followers. Jesus shared bread with them. Catholics believe that Jesus is in the special bread they share at church. On this day they celebrate him in a special way. Parades with songs walk through the streets of many towns. In Portugal this is a day off.
pt-corpo-deus.q: On which day of the week is this holiday?
pt-corpo-deus.draw: Draw a happy parade along an old street in a town

pt-dia-portugal.kid: The tenth of June is Portugal Day. It is the day of the poet Camões. It is also the day of all Portuguese people who live in countries around the world. Luís de Camões lived more than four hundred years ago. He wrote the poem “The Lusiads”. It tells how the sailor Vasco da Gama sailed his ships all the way to India. This day was chosen to remember the poet. There are special ceremonies and concerts, and Portuguese people all over the world come together.
pt-dia-portugal.q: What is the poem “The Lusiads” about?
a: How a soup ran away from its pot
A dragon who was afraid of mice
pt-dia-portugal.draw: Draw an old ship with white sails on the open sea

pt-santo-antonio.kid: Saint Anthony was born in Lisbon more than eight hundred years ago. He is the favourite saint of the city. People say he helps people who are in love, so many weddings take place in Lisbon at this time. On the night before the thirteenth of June, the “marchas” walk along Avenida da Liberdade. They are happy parades from different parts of the city, in bright costumes. People grill sardines in the streets. People in love get a little pot of basil with a paper carnation and a poem. The thirteenth of June is a day off in Lisbon.
pt-santo-antonio.q: What do people give to their loved ones on Saint Anthony’s Day?
pt-santo-antonio.draw: Draw a little pot of basil with a paper carnation

pt-sao-joao.kid: On the night between the twenty-third and twenty-fourth of June, the city of Porto celebrates Saint John’s Day. All night people walk in the streets. For fun, they tap each other on the head with soft plastic hammers. People grill sardines everywhere and give little pots of basil as gifts. At midnight, big fireworks go boom over the River Douro. The twenty-fourth of June is a day off in Porto.
pt-sao-joao.q: What do people tap each other on the head with, for fun?
pt-sao-joao.draw: Draw a colourful plastic hammer and fireworks over the river

pt-assuncao.kid: On the fifteenth of August, Catholics remember the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus. They believe that God took her up to heaven. In these days, villages and small towns in Portugal have summer parties with parades, music, dancing, fairs and fireworks in the evening. Many Portuguese people who live in other countries come home in August to see their families. It is a day off for the whole country.
pt-assuncao.q: Who comes home to Portugal in August?
a: Portuguese people who live in other countries
pt-assuncao.draw: Draw a summer village fair with little flags and fireworks

pt-republica.kid: More than a hundred years ago, on the fifth of October, Portugal stopped having a king. It became a republic, a country with a president. From the balcony of Lisbon’s town hall, people heard the news. From now on, a president would run the country, not a king. Soon Portugal had a new flag, green and red. Every year on this day the flag goes up at the town hall and the national song plays. It is a day off.
pt-republica.q: Who started running Portugal instead of the king?
a: A cook with a big spoon
pt-republica.draw: Draw the flag of Portugal — green and red

pt-halloween.kid: Halloween, or the Day of the Witches (“Dia das Bruxas” in Portuguese), came to Portugal from other countries. Schools love it most. Children dress up as funny little witches, cats and pumpkins. Classes have costume parties. People cut happy lanterns with smiling faces out of pumpkins. It is not a day off, just a fun game at the end of October.
pt-halloween.q: What do you carve out of pumpkins?
pt-halloween.draw: Draw a cheerful pumpkin lantern with a smile

pt-todos-santos.kid: On the first of November, Catholics remember all the saints. They also remember loved ones who are no longer with them, and bring them flowers. Children have an old tradition of their own. In the morning they go round to the neighbours with cloth bags and say “Pão por Deus”, which means “bread, for God’s sake”. The neighbours put bread, rolls, nuts, sweets and pomegranates into the bags. In some places this day is even called the day of the rolls. It is a day off in Portugal.
pt-todos-santos.q: What do children take with them when they go round the neighbours?
pt-todos-santos.draw: Draw a cloth bag full of rolls, nuts and pomegranates

pt-sao-martinho.kid: The eleventh of November is Saint Martin’s Day. There is an old story. On a cold, rainy day, a Roman soldier called Martin met a poor man. Martin cut his cloak in half and gave the man one half. Just then, the sun came out! That is why warm days in November in Portugal are called “Saint Martin’s summer”. On this day people roast chestnuts everywhere. Schools have a chestnut party, and in the streets people sell hot chestnuts in paper cones.
pt-sao-martinho.q: What did Martin give to the poor man?
pt-sao-martinho.draw: Draw roasted chestnuts in a paper cone

pt-restauracao.kid: Long ago, kings from Spain ruled Portugal for sixty years. Almost four hundred years ago, on the first of December, a group of brave Portuguese people said that Portugal would have its own king again. His name was John the Fourth. So Portugal was free again. In Lisbon, there is a square named after these brave people. A tall stone monument stands in it. It is a day off.
pt-restauracao.q: Who became king of Portugal on the first of December?
pt-restauracao.draw: Draw a crown and a flag next to a tall stone monument

pt-imaculada.kid: On the eighth of December, Catholics remember the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus. On this holiday they say she is the special protector of Portugal. Almost four hundred years ago, King John the Fourth laid his crown at her statue. People say that after that, the kings of Portugal never wore a crown again. Christmas is not far away now, and the streets glow with lights. It is a day off.
pt-imaculada.q: What did King John the Fourth do with his crown?
a: Put it down at the statue of the Virgin Mary
Made a soup bowl out of it
Gave it to the neighbour’s hen
pt-imaculada.draw: Draw a golden crown with stars around it

pt-consoada.kid: On the evening of the twenty-fourth of December, Portuguese families come together for the Christmas supper, the “consoada”. On the table there is always cod with potatoes and cabbage. For pudding there is sweet French toast and doughnuts. Children put a little shoe by the fireplace or under the tree, hoping to find a gift in it. At midnight many people go to church for the special Christmas service called the “Rooster’s Mass”.
pt-consoada.q: Which fish is always eaten at the Christmas supper in Portugal?
pt-consoada.draw: Draw a little shoe by the fireplace with a gift inside

pt-natal.kid: On the twenty-fifth of December, Christians celebrate Christmas, the day when Jesus was born. In homes and churches in Portugal, people set up a nativity scene. It has little figures of Mary, Joseph, a donkey and an ox around a manger. On Christmas night, people put the figure of baby Jesus in the manger. Pai Natal, the Portuguese Father Christmas, brings the children’s gifts. In some families, they say baby Jesus brings the gifts himself. During the day the whole family comes together for a big lunch.
pt-natal.q: When is the figure of baby Jesus put in the manger?
pt-natal.draw: Draw a nativity scene: a manger, a little donkey, an ox and a bright star above them

pt-ano-novo.kid: On the night of the first of January, the Portuguese welcome the New Year. When the clock strikes twelve, many people eat twelve raisins, one for each bong, and make twelve wishes. Fireworks boom in the sky. People hug each other and say happy New Year. The first of January is a day off, and everyone rests after a fun night.
pt-ano-novo.q: How many raisins do people eat as the clock strikes?
a: Just one, but as big as a watermelon
pt-ano-novo.draw: Draw a clock showing midnight and fireworks over the sea

pt-cascais.kid: On the thirteenth of June, the city of Cascais has its city holiday. It is Saint Anthony’s Day, and it is a day off. On the seventh of June Cascais has its birthday. More than six hundred years ago, King Pedro the First made it a town of its own, not part of nearby Sintra any more. That is why Cascais has a whole week of parties in June. On the thirteenth of June, a parade for Saint Anthony goes through the streets.
pt-cascais.q: Whose day is celebrated on the thirteenth of June in Cascais?
pt-cascais.draw: Draw a lighthouse, boats and festive little flags on the seashore

ru-kanikuly.kid: From the first to the eighth of January, Russia has its longest winter holiday. Grown-ups and children all rest. Under the New Year tree you find gifts from Father Frost and the Snow Maiden. Everyone goes sledging and skating, builds snowmen and visits friends. Grandpas and grannies are very happy when their grandchildren phone them and say happy New Year.
ru-kanikuly.q: Who brings the presents under the New Year tree in Russia?
a: Father Frost and the Snow Maiden
ru-kanikuly.draw: Draw a snowman with a carrot nose and a sledge next to him

ru-rozhdestvo.kid: On the seventh of January, Orthodox Christians celebrate Christmas, the day when Jesus was born. The Russian Orthodox Church uses the old calendar. So Christmas in Russia comes almost two weeks later than in Portugal. On the evening before, Christmas Eve, people wait for the first star in the sky. Only then do they sit down to the big supper. Children dress up and go from house to house. They sing songs called “kolyadki” and get sweets for it.
ru-rozhdestvo.q: What do people wait for on Christmas Eve before they sit down to supper?
ru-rozhdestvo.draw: Draw the first star above a snow-covered little house

ru-staryi-novyi-god.kid: Long ago, people in Russia used the old calendar. By that calendar, the New Year comes on the night between the thirteenth and fourteenth of January. The calendar was changed long ago, but the holiday stayed. People celebrate once more, at home, in a cosy way. Many keep the New Year tree up until this day. They sit around the party table again. So you can welcome the New Year twice! It is not a day off.
ru-staryi-novyi-god.q: How many times can you welcome the New Year in Russia?
ru-staryi-novyi-god.draw: Draw two Christmas trees: one for New Year and the other for Old New Year

ru-23-fevralya.kid: On the twenty-third of February in Russia, people thank those who protect the country, the soldiers. On this day they say happy holiday to all dads, grandpas, brothers and boys. Children draw cards and make gifts with their hands. In big cities there are sometimes fireworks in the evening. It is a day off.
ru-23-fevralya.q: Who gets good wishes on the twenty-third of February?
a: Only the fish in the aquarium
ru-23-fevralya.draw: Draw a card for Dad or Grandpa

ru-maslenitsa.kid: Maslenitsa is a fun week for saying goodbye to winter. It comes before Lent, the quiet time before Easter. All week people make pancakes, round and golden like the sun. They eat them with sour cream, honey and jam. People slide down hills, dance in circles and have snowball fights. On the last day they say sorry to each other and forgive each other. At the party they burn a straw doll of Maslenitsa. That is how they say goodbye to winter.
ru-maslenitsa.draw: Draw a stack of pancakes with jam

ru-8-marta.kid: The eighth of March is a holiday for all mums, grannies, sisters, women teachers and girls. People give them flowers: tulips and fluffy yellow mimosa. Children make cards and help Mum at home. In Russia it is a day off.
ru-8-marta.q: What flowers are given on the eighth of March?
ru-8-marta.draw: Draw a sprig of yellow mimosa for Mum

ru-kosmonavtiki.kid: More than sixty years ago, on the twelfth of April, Yuri Gagarin was the first person to fly into space. His spaceship was called “Vostok”. Gagarin flew all the way round the Earth and came back in less than two hours. Before take-off he said happily: “Let’s go!” Today, on this day, people remember all the cosmonauts, and children make rockets out of cardboard.
ru-kosmonavtiki.q: What did Gagarin say before take-off?
ru-kosmonavtiki.draw: Draw a rocket flying to the stars

ru-paskha.kid: Easter is the biggest holiday for Orthodox Christians. They are happy that Jesus Christ rose again. That means he came back to life. The day before, people colour eggs and bake tall Easter cakes called kulich. They take them to church to be blessed. When people meet, one says “Christ is risen!” and the other answers “Truly he is risen!” Children love to knock their coloured eggs together. Whoever’s egg stays whole wins.
ru-paskha.q: What do people reply to the words “Christ is risen!”?
ru-paskha.draw: Draw a kulich and colourful eggs

ru-1-maya.kid: The first of May is the holiday of spring and work. It is a day for everyone who works. In Russia it is a day off. Many families go to their dacha, a little house in the countryside. They plant flowers and vegetables and have picnics. In the cities there are happy marches with balloons and little flags. Everything around turns green and flowers come out.
ru-1-maya.q: Where do many families go on the first of May?
a: To the Moon on a bicycle
ru-1-maya.draw: Draw a dacha with flowerbeds and flowers

ru-pobeda.kid: More than eighty years ago the Great Patriotic War ended. This is what the Second World War is called in Russia. It was a very big and terrible war. On the ninth of May people remember those who defended their country and brought peace. They say thank you to the veterans, the people who fought in the war. People put flowers at monuments and at the Eternal Flame. Many tell children about their great-grandfathers and great-grandmothers. In the evening, fireworks light up the sky. It is a day off.
ru-pobeda.q: Where do people bring flowers on the ninth of May?
a: To monuments and to the Eternal Flame
Onto the roof of a bus
ru-pobeda.draw: Draw red carnations and festive fireworks in the sky

ru-den-peterburga.kid: More than three hundred years ago, Tsar Peter the Great built a new city by the River Neva. It was Saint Petersburg. The first thing he built was the Peter and Paul Fortress on Hare Island. Every year on the twenty-seventh of May the city has its birthday. There are concerts, parties and street fairs. Petersburg is famous for its bridges that lift up and for its white nights, when it hardly gets dark in summer.
ru-den-peterburga.q: What is the island called where the first fortress was built?
ru-den-peterburga.draw: Draw a bridge that lifts up over the river, with a little boat under it

ru-zashchita-detei.kid: The first of June is Children’s Protection Day, a holiday for all children. Grown-ups remind us that we must keep children safe and look after them. In parks there are concerts and games. Children draw with chalk on the pavement. It is also the first day of summer!
ru-zashchita-detei.q: What do children draw on the pavement with?
ru-zashchita-detei.draw: Draw the sun and a rainbow, as if with chalk on the pavement

ru-den-rossii.kid: The twelfth of June is Russia Day, one of the biggest holidays in the country. On this day, more than thirty years ago, people agreed on an important paper that began the Russia of today. White, blue and red flags wave everywhere. There are concerts in the cities, and fireworks in the evening. It is a day off.
ru-den-rossii.q: What colours is the flag of Russia?
ru-den-rossii.draw: Draw the flag of Russia and festive fireworks

ru-den-semyi.kid: On the eighth of July, Russia celebrates the Day of Family, Love and Being True. It is the day of Peter and Fevronia, a prince and a wise girl from the city of Murom. You can read about them in an old tale. Fevronia made Prince Peter well when he was ill. They got married and lived a long and happy life together. The holiday has a flower as its sign: the daisy. So on this day families give each other daisies.
ru-den-semyi.q: Which flower is the sign of Family Day?
ru-den-semyi.draw: Draw your family and a big daisy

ru-den-znanii.kid: The first of September is Knowledge Day. The school year begins in Russia. Pupils put on smart uniforms and bring bunches of flowers for their teachers. There is a special assembly in the school yard, and the first bell rings. The youngest pupils feel a bit nervous, because it is their very first school day.
ru-den-znanii.q: What rings at the special assembly?
a: An alarm clock in a cat’s backpack
ru-den-znanii.draw: Draw a schoolbag and a bunch of flowers for the teacher

ru-edinstvo.kid: More than four hundred years ago, an army from another country took over Moscow. Then people from many cities joined Kuzma Minin, a trader, and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky. Together they freed Moscow. On the fourth of November we remember that when people work together, they can beat any trouble. In Red Square there is a monument to Minin and Pozharsky. It is a day off.
ru-edinstvo.q: Who led the people to free Moscow?
ru-edinstvo.draw: Draw people from different cities holding hands

ru-den-materi.kid: On the last Sunday of November, Russia celebrates Mother’s Day. Children draw cards for their mums and make gifts with their hands. They say kind words. You can make Mum breakfast, help her at home, or just give her a big hug. It is nice to phone Granny too. After all, she is the mum of your mum or dad!
ru-den-materi.q: What can you do for Mum on this day?
a: Give her a big, tight hug
Hide her slippers in the freezer
ru-den-materi.draw: Draw a portrait of Mum with flowers

ru-kanun-novogo-goda.kid: On the thirty-first of December, the whole of Russia gets ready to welcome the New Year. People decorate the tree and make salads, and the table smells of tangerines. At midnight the big clock on the Spasskaya Tower of the Kremlin rings. These are the Kremlin clock bells. While they ring, everyone makes a wish. Then everybody says happy New Year to each other, and fireworks burst in the sky. In Moscow the New Year comes three hours earlier than in Lisbon. So grandparents in Russia welcome it earlier than in Portugal!
ru-kanun-novogo-goda.q: Where does the New Year come first — in Moscow or in Lisbon?
a: At the bottom of the sea, with the crabs
ru-kanun-novogo-goda.draw: Draw a New Year tree, tangerines and a clock showing midnight

newyear.kid: New Year is the first day of the new year. At midnight people say happy New Year to each other, watch fireworks and make wishes. In Spain, people eat twelve grapes as the clock strikes, one grape for each bong.
newyear.q: When does the new year begin?
newyear.draw: Draw festive fireworks over a city at night.

threekings.kid: On this day people remember how three wise men, the Magi, came with gifts to baby Jesus. In Spain the three kings bring children presents in the night. In the morning everyone eats a round cake with a surprise inside. In Italy a kind old lady called Befana puts sweets in children's stockings.
threekings.q: Who brings children presents in Spain on this day?
threekings.draw: Draw the three kings on camels, following a bright star.

epiphany.kid: On this day people remember how Jesus was baptised in the River Jordan. Priests bless the water, and people take some home. In Greece and Cyprus a priest throws a cross into the sea, and brave swimmers dive in to get it.
epiphany.q: What does the priest throw into the sea in Greece on this day?
epiphany.draw: Draw a white dove above the blue water.

goodfriday.kid: This is a quiet, sad day before Easter. Christians remember how Jesus died on the cross, and they go to church. In Spain slow, quiet parades walk through the streets, and in Britain people eat sweet buns with a cross on top.
goodfriday.q: Which buns do people eat in Britain on this day?
goodfriday.draw: Draw a bun with a cross on top and spring flowers next to it.

easter.kid: Easter is the biggest Christian holiday. People are happy that Jesus rose again. Children look in the garden for hidden chocolate eggs. They say the Easter bunny brings them. Families paint eggs and sit together at the party table.
easter.q: Who, according to the story, hides the Easter eggs?
easter.draw: Draw a basket of colourful Easter eggs.

eastermonday.kid: This is the second day of Easter, and the party goes on. Families visit friends, go for walks outside and play with eggs, like rolling them down a hill. In Poland, on this day everybody has fun splashing each other with water.
eastermonday.q: What fun thing do people do in Poland on Easter Monday?
a: They splash each other with water
They sprinkle each other with flour
eastermonday.draw: Draw colourful eggs rolling down a hill.

ascension.kid: Forty days after Easter, Christians remember how Jesus went up to heaven. This holiday is always on a Thursday, and many families go away for a long weekend. In Germany, Father's Day is on this day too.
ascension.q: On which day of the week is Ascension always?
ascension.draw: Draw a blue sky with white clouds and sunbeams.

pentecost.kid: Fifty days after Easter, Christians remember how the Holy Spirit came down to Jesus's followers. So the holiday is also called Pentecost. Homes and churches are decorated with green branches and flowers. In Poland that is just what it is called: the Green Holidays.
pentecost.q: What do people decorate their homes with at Trinity?
pentecost.draw: Draw a house decorated with green branches and flowers.

whitmonday.kid: This is the Monday right after Trinity, the second day of the holiday. Grown-ups rest. Families go for walks, go out into the countryside and have picnics. In Cyprus on this day there is a happy party by the sea where everyone splashes each other with water.
whitmonday.q: What do many families do on Holy Spirit Day?
whitmonday.draw: Draw a family picnic on a green meadow.

corpuschristi.kid: This Catholic holiday is on a Thursday, sixty days after Easter. Parades walk through the streets, and children in white clothes throw flower petals on the road in front of them. The road is decorated with flowers and birch branches.
corpuschristi.q: What do the children throw in front of the parade?
corpuschristi.draw: Draw a path of colourful petals.

labour.kid: This is a holiday for everyone who works: doctors, builders, cooks, drivers and teachers. In many countries it is on the first of May, and in America it is at the start of September. People go out to happy parades, and then rest with their families.
labour.q: Who gets good wishes on Workers’ Day?
labour.draw: Draw what you want to be when you grow up.

assumption.kid: On this summer day Christians remember the Virgin Mary, the mum of Jesus. People go to church and bring flowers and herbs. Many towns have parties with music. In Italy it is also the middle of summer, when almost everyone goes to the seaside.
assumption.q: Who do people remember on this day?
assumption.draw: Draw a bunch of summer flowers and herbs.

allsaints.kid: On this autumn day people remember the saints and loved ones who are no longer with us. Families take flowers to the cemetery, mostly chrysanthemums, and light candles. In Poland, in the evening, thousands of little lights glow in the cemeteries.
allsaints.q: Which flowers are often brought on this day?
allsaints.draw: Draw an autumn evening with the warm glow of candles.

christmaseve.kid: This is the evening before Christmas. In Poland children watch the sky for the first star. Only then does the family sit down to the big supper. Everyone shares a thin wafer and says kind wishes to each other. An extra plate is left on the table for a guest who might come by surprise.
christmaseve.q: What do children in Poland wait for before sitting down at the table?
christmaseve.draw: Draw the first evening star above a snowy house.

christmas.kid: Christmas is the birthday of Jesus Christ. At home people decorate the tree. The whole family sits around the party table, and everyone gives each other presents. Children wait for Santa Claus. He leaves presents at night under the tree or in a stocking.
christmas.q: Whose birthday is celebrated at Christmas?
christmas.draw: Draw a Christmas tree with presents under it.

christmas2.kid: Christmas is so big that it lasts two days. Families visit their relatives, go for walks and finish the yummy treats. In Italy on this day people remember Saint Stephen. In Greece and Cyprus they remember the Virgin Mary.
christmas2.q: How many days is Christmas celebrated in these countries?
christmas2.draw: Draw yourself going to visit Granny with a present.

boxing.kid: This is the day after Christmas. Long ago, on this day people gave boxes of presents to postmen and to everyone who had helped them all year. Today people go for walks, watch football and go shopping.
boxing.q: Who used to be given boxes of presents on this day?
boxing.draw: Draw a box with a present, tied with a ribbon.

orthchristmas.kid: Orthodox Christians celebrate the birthday of Jesus Christ in winter, after New Year. The evening before, they wait for the first star, and at night they go to church. In Serbia people bake a special bread with a coin inside. In Georgia a happy Alilo parade goes through the streets.
orthchristmas.q: What is hidden in the Serbian Christmas bread?
orthchristmas.draw: Draw the Christmas star above a little church.

orthgoodfriday.kid: This is the quietest and saddest day before Easter. Orthodox Christians remember how Jesus was hurt and died on the cross. People go to church with candles. In many families they colour Easter eggs in these days.
orthgoodfriday.q: What do many families colour before Easter?
orthgoodfriday.draw: Draw a candle and a red Easter egg.

holysaturday.kid: This is the last day before Easter. Families bake special bread, finish colouring the eggs and tidy the house. Late in the evening many people go to church for the night-time Easter service.
holysaturday.q: What do people bake on Holy Saturday?
holysaturday.draw: Draw a special basket with bread and coloured eggs.

ortheaster.kid: Easter is the most important holiday for Orthodox Christians. They are glad that Jesus has risen. At night they go to church with candles. Then they say to each other: “Christ is risen!” — “Truly He is risen!” Everyone knocks coloured eggs together to see whose is stronger. They eat sweet Easter bread too.
ortheaster.q: What is the reply to “Christ is risen!”?
ortheaster.draw: Draw coloured Easter eggs and a sweet Easter bread.

cleanmonday.kid: From this day Orthodox Christians begin Great Lent. This is a time of getting ready for Easter. In Greece and Cyprus everyone goes out into the countryside, eats flatbread and vegetables and flies kites in the sky. In Cyprus this day is called Green Monday.
cleanmonday.q: What do people fly into the sky on Clean Monday?
cleanmonday.draw: Draw a bright kite in the sky.

immaculate.kid: This is a Catholic holiday for the Virgin Mary, the mum of Jesus. Christians believe that from the very start of her life she was especially good and kind. People go to church. In Italy, on this day, they start to decorate Christmas trees.
immaculate.q: What do people in Italy start doing on this day?
immaculate.draw: Draw a family decorating a Christmas tree.

womensday.kid: On this spring day we say happy holiday to all women and girls: mums, grannies, sisters and teachers. They get flowers, like tulips and mimosa, and cards and presents made by hand. It is a good time to tell Mum how much you love her.
womensday.q: Who gets good wishes on Women's Day?
womensday.draw: Draw a card with tulips for Mum.

victory.kid: In the spring of 1945 a very big and scary war ended. On this day people remember everyone who fought and died. They thank the veterans, the soldiers who fought long ago. People bring flowers to monuments. They wish there will never be a war again.
victory.q: What do people bring to monuments on Victory Day?
victory.draw: Draw a white dove of peace with a little twig in its beak.

armistice.kid: More than a hundred years ago, in 1918, the First World War ended. At eleven o'clock in the morning the guns went quiet. On this day people remember the soldiers who died. They put flowers at monuments. In France people wear a blue cornflower. In Serbia they wear a purple ramonda flower.
armistice.q: At what time did the guns go quiet at the end of that war?
a: At eleven o'clock in the morning
armistice.draw: Draw a blue cornflower to help us remember.

independence.kid: On this day a country celebrates being free. Long ago it became its own country and chose its own way to live. It is like the country's birthday. Flags hang everywhere. There are parades and concerts. In the evening, fireworks go bang in the sky.
independence.q: What is Independence Day like for a country?
independence.draw: Draw the flag of the country where you live, and some fireworks.

nationalday.kid: This is the biggest holiday of the country. People remember something big from long ago that makes them proud. Flags wave in the streets. There are parades, concerts and fairs. In the evening there are often fireworks.
nationalday.q: What waves in the streets on National Day?
nationalday.draw: Draw a street full of flags for the party.

constitution.kid: A constitution is the main law of a country. It says what every person is allowed to do. It also says what rules the whole country follows. On this day people hang out flags and go to concerts.
a: The main law of a country
constitution.draw: Draw a big book of rules you would make for your family.

greek-independence.kid: On the twenty-fifth of March 1821 the Greeks began to fight to make their country free. On this day the church also remembers the Annunciation, when an angel told Mary happy news. Schoolchildren march in parades with blue-and-white flags. For lunch people eat fried fish with garlic sauce.
greek-independence.q: What colour is the flag of Greece?
greek-independence.draw: Draw the blue-and-white flag of Greece.

ochi.kid: On the twenty-eighth of October 1940 Greece said a loud “No!” — in Greek, “Ochi!” — when an army from another country wanted to come in. The Greeks and Cypriots are proud of how brave they were. On this day schoolchildren march in parades. The streets have blue-and-white flags.
ochi.q: What does the Greek word “Ochi” mean?
ochi.draw: Draw schoolchildren at a parade with blue-and-white flags.

halloween.kid: Halloween is on the last evening of October. Children dress up in funny and scary costumes. They go from house to house and say “Trick or treat!” The neighbours give them sweets. People cut happy faces into pumpkins to make lanterns.
halloween.q: What do people make from a pumpkin at Halloween?
halloween.draw: Draw a pumpkin lantern with a happy face.

thanksgiving.kid: On this autumn day American families sit round a big table. They say thank you for all the good things of the year. There is roast turkey and pumpkin pie to eat. Every year the President of America lets one turkey go free, as a joke. It goes to live on a farm.
thanksgiving.q: Which bird is roasted for Thanksgiving?
thanksgiving.draw: Draw round your hand and make it into a turkey with a colourful tail.

nowruz.kid: Nowruz is the holiday when spring comes. It is also the start of the new year in the old calendar. On this day the day and the night are the same length. People wear their best clothes, put up yurts, sing and play old games. In Kazakhstan it is called Nauryz. People cook nauryz-kozhe, a soup made from seven foods.
nowruz.q: What are people happy about at Nowruz?
nowruz.draw: Draw a yurt and the spring sun over the grassy plain.

eid-fitr.kid: For a whole month, called Ramadan, grown-up Muslims do not eat or drink from sunrise to sunset. Eid al-Fitr is a happy holiday at the end of that month. People pray, wear new clothes and visit each other. Children get treats and presents.
eid-fitr.q: What treats do children get at Eid al-Fitr?
eid-fitr.draw: Draw a thin moon and a star above the houses.

eid-adha.kid: This is one of the biggest Muslim holidays. People remember the story of the prophet Ibrahim, who believed in God with all his heart. They pray and visit each other. They always share party food with their neighbours and with people who are having a hard time.
eid-adha.q: Who do people usually share food with at Eid al-Adha?
a: With neighbours and with people who are having a hard time
eid-adha.draw: Draw a big party table with guests round it.

newyear-hijri.kid: Today the new year begins in the Islamic calendar. This calendar follows the Moon. Its years start from the time the prophet Muhammad moved from the city of Mecca to the city of Medina. It is a quiet holiday. People pray and wish each other a good year.
newyear-hijri.q: How is the Islamic calendar counted?
newyear-hijri.draw: Draw a thin moon above the desert and a line of camels.

mawlid.kid: On this day Muslims remember when the prophet Muhammad was born. People tell stories about his life and how kind he was. They read poems and prayers. In many places people light up lanterns and share sweets.
mawlid.q: What do people light up in many places on this day?

rosh-hashanah.kid: Rosh Hashanah is the Jewish New Year. It lasts two days in autumn. People dip pieces of apple in honey, so the year will be sweet. In the synagogue people blow the shofar, a big horn from a ram.
rosh-hashanah.q: What is the apple dipped into at Rosh Hashanah?
rosh-hashanah.draw: Draw a red apple and a little jar of honey.

yom-kippur.kid: Yom Kippur is the most important day of the year for Jews. Grown-ups do not eat all day. They pray and say sorry to each other. In Israel no cars drive on this day, so children ride bicycles on the empty roads.
yom-kippur.q: What do children ride along the empty roads of Israel on Yom Kippur?
yom-kippur.draw: Draw an empty road with children riding bicycles along it.

sukkot.kid: At Sukkot people build huts from branches. They decorate them with fruit and paper chains. This is to remember something from long, long ago. The Jewish people walked through the desert for forty years and lived in huts. For a whole week people eat in the hut, and some even sleep in it.
sukkot.q: What do people build for the holiday of Sukkot?
sukkot.draw: Draw a hut made of branches, decorated with fruit.

pesach.kid: Passover is the holiday of freedom. Jews remember how their people left Egypt, where they were slaves. All week they eat thin, crunchy bread called matzah. At the party supper children ask questions and look for a hidden piece of matzah.
pesach.q: What bread do people eat at Passover?
pesach.draw: Draw a festive table with matzah.

hanukkah.kid: Hanukkah is the festival of light. It lasts eight days. Every evening people light one more candle on a special candlestick. Children play with a spinning top, eat doughnuts and potato pancakes, and get small presents.
hanukkah.q: How many days does Hanukkah last?
hanukkah.draw: Draw a candlestick with eight burning candles.

4.kid: On the first of April 1955 the people of Cyprus began to fight so that Britain would no longer be in charge of their country. On this day people remember the heroes who fought. Schoolchildren march in parades with flags. People read poems and sing songs by the monuments.
4.q: Who marches in the parades on this day?
4.draw: Draw a school parade with flags.

6.kid: For many years Germany was two countries. A high wall also cut the city of Berlin in two. In 1989 the wall was opened. On the third of October 1990 the country became one again. On this day there are parties with music, flags and treats.
6.q: What cut the city of Berlin in two for many years?
6.draw: Draw people from the two halves of the city hugging by the wall.

4.kid: In the spring of 1945, at the end of the big war, Italy became free. It was freed from soldiers who had come in, and from cruel rulers who had taken away people's freedom. On this day people bring flowers to monuments, enjoy the parties and sing songs about freedom.
4.q: What are Italians happy about on this day?
4.draw: Draw a square where people sing songs under flags.

7.kid: Saint Francis is the saint who looks after Italy. He lived long, long ago in the city of Assisi. He was very kind. He called everyone his brothers and sisters: people, birds, animals, the sun and the moon. Since 2026 this day is a day off in Italy again.
7.q: Who did Saint Francis call brothers and sisters?
7.draw: Draw Saint Francis feeding the birds.

3.kid: On the first Monday of May all of England has a day off. People say hello to spring. They dance round a tall maypole with long colourful ribbons. Dancers with bells on their legs do old dances. Sometimes they pick a May queen.
3.q: What do people dance around in England in spring?
3.draw: Draw a maypole with colourful ribbons.

4.kid: This is a day off on the last Monday of May. Families walk in parks, go to the seaside and have picnics. In one English village there is a funny race on this day. People run down a steep hill after a rolling wheel of cheese.
4.q: What do people chase down the hill in the English village?
4.draw: Draw a wheel of cheese rolling down a hill, and the people running after it.

5.kid: This is the last summer day off before school, on the last Monday of August. Families go to the seaside, eat ice cream and go for walks. In London at this time there is a huge carnival with music, drums and bright costumes.
5.q: What happens in London at this time?
5.draw: Draw a bright carnival costume with feathers.

1.kid: Martin Luther King had a dream. He dreamed that people of every skin colour would be treated the same. He fought for this in a peaceful way, with words, songs and marches. On this day Americans remember his famous speech “I Have a Dream”. They also help other people.
1.q: What did Martin Luther King dream of?
a: That all people would be treated the same
That it would be summer in winter
That everyone would have their own dinosaur
1.draw: Draw children from all over the world holding hands.

2.kid: This is George Washington's birthday. He was the first President of America. Many people call it Presidents' Day. They remember everyone who has led the country. A story says that little Washington cut down a cherry tree, and then he told the truth about it.
2.q: Who was the first President of America?
2.draw: Draw a picture of a president in a tall hat.

3.kid: On this day Americans remember the soldiers who died to keep their country safe. People bring flowers and little flags to monuments. It is also the start of summer. Many families go to the beach or have a picnic for the first time this year.
3.q: What is brought to the monuments on Memorial Day?
3.draw: Draw a little flag next to a bunch of flowers.

4.kid: Long, long ago in America many Black people were slaves. They were not free. On the nineteenth of June 1865 the last of them, in the state of Texas, heard that they were free now. Since then people celebrate this day with music, parades and family lunches.
4.q: What are people happy about on this day?
4.draw: Draw a happy parade with musicians.

7.kid: In 1492 a sailor called Christopher Columbus sailed across the ocean with three ships and reached America. On this day people remember his trip. Many Americans also show respect to the first peoples who lived in America long before Columbus.
7.q: How many ships did Columbus have?
7.draw: Draw three ships with sails in the middle of the ocean.

9.kid: On this day Americans say “thank you” to everyone who has been in their country's army. Veterans are invited to schools and get cards. There are parades in the streets. The holiday is on the eleventh of November. That is the day in 1918 when the First World War ended.
9.q: Who is told “thank you” on Veterans Day?
a: Those who were in the army
9.draw: Draw a card with the words “thank you” for a veteran.

3.kid: On this day the Netherlands celebrates the king's birthday. The whole country wears orange. In the streets there is a huge fair. Children sell their old toys and show what they can do. Boats with music float along the canals.
3.q: What colour does the whole country dress in on King's Day?
3.draw: Draw yourself in an orange crown.

4.kid: Petar Petrović Njegoš was the ruler of Montenegro and a great poet. He was born in the autumn of 1813. He wrote the famous poem “The Mountain Wreath”. On this day people read his poems. Many climb Mount Lovćen, where he is buried.
4.q: Who was Njegoš, besides being a ruler?
4.draw: Draw a tall mountain and a poet with a feather pen in his hand.

3.kid: In Georgia on this day everyone says happy holiday to all mums. Children give them flowers, drawings and cards. Grown-ups visit their mums and say kind words to them. It is a day to hug Mum and say “thank you”.
3.q: What can you give Mum on this day?
3.draw: Draw a picture of your mum with flowers.

5.kid: On the ninth of April 1989 in Tbilisi people went out into the streets without fighting, because they wanted their country to be free. Some of them died. On this day people remember them and bring flowers. Two years later, on the same day, Georgia said it was a free country of its own.
5.q: What do people bring to the monument on this day?
5.draw: Draw a bunch of flowers and a burning candle.

11.kid: Andrew the First-Called was one of Jesus's first helpers. People say that he came to Georgia and told people about Jesus. On this day Georgians go to church and remember his long trip.
11.draw: Draw a traveller walking along a mountain road.

12.kid: On this day in Georgia people talk about how important family is. Children say thank you to Mum and Dad, grannies and grandpas. Families spend time together. Many have a party lunch and go for a walk all together.
12.q: Whom do children thank on this day?

15.kid: This is the holiday of Svetitskhoveli Cathedral in the very old city of Mtskheta. Long ago it was the capital of Georgia. People say that a robe of Jesus Christ is kept there. On this day many people come to Mtskheta. There is a church service in the cathedral and a big party in the town.
15.q: In which city is Svetitskhoveli Cathedral?
15.draw: Draw an old cathedral on the river bank.

16.kid: This is the day of Saint George, who looks after Georgia from heaven. In icons he is painted on a white horse, beating a dragon. On this day people go to church. Everyone called Giorgi gets happy wishes. It is one of the best-loved names in Georgia.
16.q: Who does Saint George beat in the icons?
16.draw: Draw a rider on a white horse and a dragon.

1.kid: The Armenian Church celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ and his baptism on the same day. On the evening before, families sit round the party table, and there are services in the churches. People greet each other with the words: “Christ is born and revealed!”
1.q: What is celebrated in Armenia on this day?
1.draw: Draw a star over an Armenian church.

2.kid: On this day in Armenia people remember all the soldiers who died to keep their country safe. People bring flowers to the monuments and say thank you to the heroes. This day of remembering began in 2026.
2.q: Who do people remember on this day?
a: Those who kept the country safe
2.draw: Draw a bunch of flowers by a monument.

3.kid: On the twenty-eighth of January, 1992, the army of Armenia was created. On this day people say happy holiday to soldiers and to everyone who has been in the army. Children give cards to their dads and grandpas. In towns there are special events and concerts.
3.q: Who do people say happy holiday to on Army Day?
a: Soldiers and everyone who was in the army
3.draw: Draw a card for Dad or Grandpa.

5.kid: This is a sad day of remembering. Armenians remember the people who died more than a hundred years ago, in 1915, in terrible times. Thousands of people climb the hill in Yerevan where a flame always burns. They bring flowers to it.
5.q: What do people bring to the flame that never goes out on this day?
5.draw: Draw spring flowers next to a candle flame.

11.kid: In Armenia the last day of the year is a day off too. Families set a party table, decorate the tree and wait for midnight. They always bake sweet, flaky gata. They put dried fruit and nuts on the table.
11.q: What sweet treat do people bake in Armenia for New Year?
11.draw: Draw a festive table with nuts and sweets.

5.kid: People from many nations live in Kazakhstan: Kazakhs, Russians, Uzbeks, Ukrainians, Koreans and many others. On this day everyone celebrates friendship together. In the squares people sing songs from different nations and dance. They share food from their own countries.
5.q: What is celebrated on this day?
5.draw: Draw children in costumes from different nations dancing in a ring.

6.kid: On the seventh of May, 1992, the army of Kazakhstan was created. On this day people say happy holiday to soldiers, dads and grandpas, everyone who keeps the country safe. Children draw cards for them and say “thank you”.
6.q: Who gets happy wishes on this day?
a: Those who keep the country safe
6.draw: Draw a card for Dad or Grandpa.

9.kid: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan. On this summer day the city has its holiday. There are concerts in the city. In the evening fireworks go boom in the sky. Many people go up the Baiterek tower. It looks like a tree with a golden egg at the top.
9.q: What does the Baiterek tower look like?
a: A tree with a golden egg
9.draw: Draw the Baiterek tower with a golden ball.

2.kid: On the twenty-third of April, 1920, the leaders of Turkey met for the first time in the Grand National Assembly. Atatürk, who started the new country of Turkey, gave this holiday to children. On this day children from different countries come to Turkey. Schoolchildren sit for a little while in the seats of the grown-up leaders.
2.q: Who did Atatürk give this holiday to?
2.draw: Draw children from different countries dancing together.

4.kid: On the nineteenth of May, 1919, Atatürk sailed to the city of Samsun. There he began the fight to make Turkey free. He gave this day to young people. In towns there are sports parties, relay races and shows by schoolchildren.
4.draw: Draw a stadium and running athletes.

6.kid: On the fifteenth of July, 2016, the people of Turkey went out into the streets to keep their country and its laws safe. On this day people remember those who died. They talk about how important it is to stay together. There are meetings to remember them all over the country, and people hang out flags.
6.q: What do people hang out on this day?
6.draw: Draw a square with red flags.

7.kid: On the thirtieth of August, 1922, the Turkish army, led by Atatürk, won the most important battle in the war for the country's freedom. On this day there are parades, and the streets have red flags. People say thank you to those who kept the country safe.
a: Red with a thin white moon and a star
7.draw: Draw a red flag with a thin white moon and a star.

1.kid: This is the last special day of Passover. People say that on this day the sea opened in two for the Jewish people. They walked across the sea floor as if it were dry land. In Israel families go for walks, go out into nature and have picnics.
1.q: In the old story, what happened to the sea on this day?
1.draw: Draw the sea opening into two walls of water.

3.kid: Shavuot comes seven weeks after Passover. On this day people remember how the Jewish people were given the Torah, a holy book. Children dress in white and wear crowns of flowers. Everyone eats foods made with milk: cheese pies and pancakes.
3.q: What food do people usually eat at Shavuot?
3.draw: Draw a crown of wild flowers.

7.kid: This is the holiday of joy for the Torah. On this day people finish reading the whole Torah. Then they start reading it again from the beginning, right away. Grown-ups and children dance with Torah scrolls. Little ones wave party flags.
7.q: What do people dance with on Simchat Torah?
7.draw: Draw a party flag for Simchat Torah.

2.kid: This is the day before Eid al-Adha. Some Muslims travel to the holy city of Mecca. On this day they gather at Mount Arafat and pray all day. Many Muslims in other places also pray, do kind things and do not eat during the day.
2.q: At which mountain do the travellers to Mecca gather on this day?
2.draw: Draw a mountain in the desert under the bright sun.
